title: trailboss --json task add
description: One row per brief: the tasks `task add` would start (no --yes), or started (--yes). With several briefs, every worktree is made before any agent starts. Started, its branch `work/<n>-<slug>` and worktree exist, made off the folder's current branch without touching that checkout, and the agent runs there in a new host terminal with the brief as its first prompt. A start that failed took its worktree and branch back (action `failed`). Frontends should show an action they don't know as is.

n.description: The task's number: what `task accept` and `task rm` take.

action.description: would start, started or failed; more may be added.

base.description: The branch it starts from, and accept merges into.

folder.description: The top of the checkout it starts from.

worktree.description: Under the folder `--worktrees` or the config's `tasks.worktrees` names (relative to the repository's top), else `worktrees/` beside the index.

host.description: herdr, tmux, …; null when no host is running (the plan then says so).

terminal.description: The new terminal's address, once started.

parent.description: AGENT:ID of the session it belongs to: the one named with --parent, else the one it was added from.

shares.description: Other tasks, added with it or open in the same folder, whose briefs name a file this brief names too: their agents may change the same file. Empty when none. A file is a word in the brief with an extension, like `src/login.rs` or `README.md`; `login.rs` and `src/login.rs` count as the same.

review.description: Whether it's reviewed before it's ready (`--review`, `--no-review`, else the config's `tasks.review`).

ignore.description: When its worktree's folder is inside the repository and git doesn't ignore it (so your checkout lists it as untracked): the line to add to the repository's .gitignore or .git/info/exclude, like `/.worktrees/`. Trailboss never writes either. Null otherwise.
